meta.phase-name: Spatial Editor UX and Project Workflow

phase-plan.purpose: Define how the project/editor workflow should expose the user's actual world model without conflating it with Space Explorer vectors or generic implementation-detail nouns.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: project sections, authored child records, import/export flow, diagnostics surfaces, and how levels, rooms, regions, floors, and related content are presented. Out of scope: final visual map editor implementation, drag placement tooling, or full room/region content creation.
phase-plan.definition-of-done: Done when the project UX shape, authored world-doc structure, and diagnostics flow are explicitly defined using the approved game-facing nouns.

file.description: Current explorer baseline that should stay focused on derived spaces and analysis rather than becoming the only world authoring tool.
Compact editor/dashboard conventions that the future spatial project UI should follow.

task.description: Define the top-level project surfaces for world authoring work.
Define how overlays and diagnostics should appear in spatial authoring.
Define import/export boundaries for level and room authored docs.

questions.question: The concrete visual editor implementation is deferred; this phase only defines the required workflow and information architecture.

decision.summary: World authoring gets a dedicated project surface rather than being hidden inside Space Explorer. The first sections should center on `Levels`, `Rooms`, `Transitions`, `Level Content`, `Diagnostics`, and `Generated Output`.
decision.impact: Prevents the analysis UI from becoming an overloaded authoring god-component and gives level/room content a first-class home in the project workflow.

decision.summary: Per-game overlays remain warnings-only in world authoring as well. They highlight missing level kinds, incomplete region composition, unsupported semantics, or incomplete content coverage without blocking edits.
decision.impact: Keeps the authoring loop fast while still showing whether a project is shaped well for a target game.

decision.summary: Level and room world docs follow the same project model as the rest of phase 56 work: live DB draft when available, import/export support, and linked child records rather than one monolithic blob.
decision.impact: World authoring can move between repo files, app drafts, and generated outputs without special-case workflow rules.

suggestion.gap: REQUIREMENTS.xml does not yet describe a first-class level/room authoring surface separate from analysis views.
suggestion.proposal: Add a requirement for dedicated world authoring sections centered on levels, rooms, transitions, diagnostics, and generated-output inspection.
